**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — no redline proposed.

The document does contain a restrictive covenant binding us — §6.1 "Exclusivity" — but it meets the playbook's fallback position on every material term:

| Fallback element | §6.1 |
|---|---|
| Named competing product | Yes — defined "Deerskin Products" + named competitors |
| During term only | Yes — no post-term tail |
| Capped at 12 months | Yes — 1-year term, 90-day termination right |
| Carve-outs | §6.2 closeout site; closeouts and Joan Cook excluded from definition |

Two points worth noting for the negotiation record, neither rising to a deviation:

1. **The asymmetry favours us.** HDI's reciprocal covenant in §6.3 runs for the term *plus two years*, while ours expires with the agreement. We should resist any attempt to "harmonise" these during redline exchange.
2. **No internal-development/acquisition carve-out.** A minor gap against the preferred position. Given the restraint reaches only online retail of a defined product set, the practical exposure is low — but if we acquire a leather-goods retailer with an existing web presence mid-term, §6.1 could arguably bite. Worth raising only if HDI opens the exclusivity section for other reasons.

The scope language "products substantially similar" and "companies similar to" is looser than ideal drafting, but it is anchored to a defined product category and a single sales channel, so it falls short of the undefined "any competing business" that would trigger walk-away treatment.
